Naming the cells rather than the chemical signal that binds the receptor.
Listing stage names without describing them.

records.context_summary: Use data to explain why diffusion suffices for a single-celled animal but a larger animal (earthworm) cannot rely on diffusion alone.
creditworthy_points: Six points: short diffusion distance in an 80 micrometre cell; diffusion fast enough (about 1.6 s); supplies oxygen or other needs; for aerobic respiration or metabolism; longer distances in the earthworm (length about 8 cm, diameter about 8 mm); diffusion too slow (about 8.7 days or 4.5 hours).
Data with the correct unit needed at least once for the full 4 marks (otherwise max 3); both organisms must be addressed.
Surface area : volume references are ignored.

[misconception] Some called Paramecium a bacterium or virus, or gave it a cell wall or a different membrane thickness. (report p.46)
[misconception] Some said earthworms need a circulatory system because they live underground. (report p.46)
[omission] Some gave a wildly small earthworm size (e.g. 8 nm). (report p.46)
